findings.evidence: "## Commit type reference" spends ~130 of ~224 lines restating conventional-commit basics ("Use `feat` for a new feature.") with placeholder examples the model reliably produces unprompted
findings.fix: Delete the section and record the removal; if users ask for it by name, move it into a skill the plugin bundles and load it by explicit path only when the notes step needs it

findings.evidence: "A release is a version of the software that is given to users." — a What-is-X section explaining releases, git, tags and semver
findings.fix: Delete the section and record the removal; the model already knows what a release, a tag and semantic versioning are

findings.evidence: "To see the history run `git log`. ... Always write clean code and good commit messages." — a git tutorial plus generic advice
findings.fix: Delete the section and record the removal; git basics and 'write clean code' are model knowledge, not release expertise

findings.evidence: Five near-identical placeholder blocks ("- First change in 1.0.0", "- First change in 1.1.0", ...) add nothing over one example
findings.fix: Keep one example as the output template, remove the other four and record the removal

findings.evidence: "1. Run the tests and make sure they pass, but do not run the tests because they are slow" — mechanical checkbox steps with no reasoning or thinking framework behind them
findings.fix: Add the expert judgment each step encodes (why the last CI run replaces running tests, what makes good release notes, when to stop) so the procedure generalises

findings.evidence: Structure mixes a tutorial, a step list, a reference dump and example outputs with no coherent pattern and no checkpoints between phases
findings.fix: Restructure as a short Process-pattern command: verify CI, draft notes, approval gate, tag and push, with the reference and example material moved out

findings.evidence: "7. Be careful and consider edge cases." — a vague warning with no content
findings.fix: Replace with specific NEVER items with reasons, e.g. 'NEVER move an already-pushed tag with `git tag -f`: consumers may have fetched it and a moved tag breaks their clones'

findings.evidence: "Never push anything before the release notes are approved by the user." — the one specific NEVER carries no reason, and there is no Gotchas section for tag or CI edge cases
findings.fix: Add the why (a pushed tag is public and hard to retract) and a Gotchas list of environment facts, e.g. what to do when the tag exists or CI has no run for this commit

findings.evidence: Frontmatter has no `description`; the host falls back to the first body line "# Release helper", which names no trigger scenario, keywords or boundaries
findings.fix: Add `description: Cut a git release: confirm the last CI run is green, draft three-sentence release notes from the commit messages, get user approval, then tag v<version> and push branch and tag. Use when asked to release, cut, ship or tag a version such as 1.2.3, even without the word 'release'. Not for CI setup or full changelog generation.`

findings.evidence: "name: cal-b" — `name` is not an accepted command field; the command name is the file name
findings.fix: Remove the `name` field; the host already names the command cal-b from commands/cal-b.md

findings.evidence: "tags: git, release" — `tags` is not in the accepted command field list; the host ignores it
findings.fix: Remove `tags`, or move it under `metadata:` (a free-form map the frontmatter accepts)

findings.evidence: ~224-line command with nothing split out: the ~130-line "## Commit type reference" and the ~50-line "## Example outputs" sit inline in the command file
findings.fix: Move the commit-type reference and the example outputs into a skill the plugin bundles, loaded by explicit path only when the notes step needs them (a command cannot ship its own references/), or delete them as model-known and record the removals

findings.evidence: "Clean up old tags and branches as needed. Use force if something is in the way, and fix whatever is broken." — maximum freedom granted to destructive remote operations
findings.fix: Give cleanup exact guarded commands (list what will be deleted and confirm with the user before any `git push --delete` or forced update), or drop cleanup from this command; destructive git operations need low freedom

findings.evidence: "id": "release-1-2-0" is the only scenario: green CI, absent tag, argument 1.2.0 — the main path alone
findings.fix: Add a failure path (last CI run red: assert the command stops before tagging; tag v1.2.0 already exists: assert the stated fallback runs) and an edge case (/cal-b with no version argument: assert it asks for the version instead of tagging literally), each with verifiable assertions

findings.evidence: "If the tag already exists, follow the steps in section \"Existing tag\" and then continue with step 9." — no section "Existing tag" exists and the list has seven steps, not nine
findings.fix: Write the actual existing-tag handling (compare `git rev-parse` of the tag with HEAD; if it points elsewhere, stop and ask) and fix the continuation step number, or delete the branch

findings.evidence: "git tag v$1" — `$N` placeholders are 0-based ($0 is the first argument), so with /cal-b 1.2.0 `$1` is a missing index and stays literal: the command would tag v$1
findings.fix: Use `v$0` (or declare `arguments: version` and write `v$version`) so /cal-b 1.2.0 produces `git tag v1.2.0`

findings.evidence: "Never push anything before the release notes are approved by the user." contradicts step 2, which pushes the branch and tag before the notes are written in step 3
findings.fix: Reorder the steps: draft the notes and pass the approval gate before any push; move step 2's `git push` commands after approval

findings.evidence: Example output "- First change in 1.0.0" (three bullets) contradicts step 3's "exactly three sentences, each starting with a verb", which the eval asserts
findings.fix: Make the kept example match the required three-sentence format, or change step 3 to the bullet format — one of the two must give

findings.evidence: "just check that the last CI run is green" — no stated outcome when the last CI run is red or missing
findings.fix: State the fallback: if CI is red or has no run for this commit, stop and report the failing job instead of releasing
